workstream: W13 judge: engineering cost and risk (research only)
status: Judgement only. Nothing under payload/, desktop/, website/, tests/, docs/ or requirements.txt was changed. This is the only file written.
lens: Engineering cost and risk: installer and SHELL_API impact (AGENTS rule 2, D3); whole-repo zipball against the 50 MiB cap; offline self-test; WebGL availability on WebView2, WKWebView, Linux and phones; CDN dependence and integrity; update path to crews (D3-D6); maintenance burden; performance plausibility; failure modes.
host_note: The product is the static website (D27; AGENTS.md:13-14). Designs A and B target the parked desktop app (DECISIONS.md:314-323). The installer, SHELL_API, zipball and self-test criteria bind only the parked app. Each design is scored on them where it touches them, and on the website equivalent for the current host.
scale: 0 = cannot be built within the written rules; 10 = lowest engineering risk on the current host, rule-compliant, with measured budgets. Scores are judgements on this lens only. The 3D capability gap is outside this lens and is noted, not scored.
method: Live: curl of cdnjs Cesium.js (sha384); WebFetch of the GitHub Actions terms, Pages limits and schedule pages; WebFetch of caniuse WebGL 2.0; PyPI JSON for eccodes 2.50.0, pygrib 2.1.8 and netCDF4 1.7.5. Local: sha256sum, wc, grep, git archive, and reads of AGENTS.md, DECISIONS.md, ROADMAP.md, website/build.py, tests/test_site.py and .github/workflows/website.yml. Reviewed evidence (review key present) was used as recorded. Unreviewed evidence was re-checked wherever a conclusion depends on it.
summary: Ranking: design C (build C2 first; C1 only as a gated later phase), then design A, then design B. C2 is the only design that runs on the current static host with no server and no new library. It has one real gap, persistence for the time window, which needs new code. Design A needs a running Flask server (D27), a CDN library that breaks AGENTS rule 4 and an existing test, and WebGL2 that is unproven on crew machines and not yet run on phones. Design B is blocked by D27, adds per-OS installers and a second server, and states a SHELL_API claim that conflicts with rule 2.

reasons: Current-host fit: a static Python build (website/build.py) published by Pages (website.yml), with no runtime server and no new library. That is what D27 chose ('no server to keep running', DECISIONS.md:353-354). The only library is vendored Leaflet 1.9.4. Its sha256 (db49d009...) matches design C and the file on disk (147,552 B, checked).

Rule 4: the six new duties N1-N6 are DOM or browser-only (layer switch, transect choice, image error, age clock, ARIA). Each needs the inline note that AGENTS.md:66-72 already requires. Total duties would be 13. map.js is already 2,155 lines (114,696 B, checked), and ROADMAP Next 9 asks to shrink it. Design C does not estimate the lines the new duties add, which is a gap in the maintenance estimate.

Publishing risk is not new. The live site already publishes MRMS and HRRR frames through Actions and Pages (D28; about 45.7 MB downloaded per build per main-architecture.json, unreviewed). The GitHub terms sentence 'You may only access and use GitHub Actions to develop and test your application(s)' was quoted live (checked). The CDN example in gh-terms-3 (hosting-options.json, unreviewed) was cut off in my live fetch. The counsel question therefore covers the whole site, not the globe increment.

Pages limits, checked live: 1 GB per site; 100 GB per month soft; a 10-minute deploy timeout (website.yml:165 uses 10). C2's 0.66 MB per visit (design budget, unmeasured) fits about 150,000 visits a month under the soft limit (computed).

Build cost: the job has a 15-minute limit (website.yml:38). The live build measured 32-51 s (main-architecture.json, unreviewed). Adding 11 MRMS levels costs about 6 s of decode (computed from 18.3 s per 33-level frame, pipeline-options.json, unreviewed) and 6.4 to 10.5 MB of download per build (design C). The 15-minute limit is not the binding constraint.

Real gap, new code needed: the rolling 7-frame echo window and the 12-frame loop cannot be built as written. load_previous fetches only data/state.json from the live site (build.py:472-478, checked), and gridded.py has no previous-frame fetch (grep, checked). Persistence needs a fetch of prior PNGs from the live site before deploy. If the live site is unreachable, the window resets and shows as a gap. Medium cost.

Test gap: CI runs four site modules (website.yml:84). Playwright is installed and run only for branch pushes (website.yml:99 and 96-105), so a map regression can reach main. Add a Chromium check for the new layers to the existing smoke pattern and run it before merge.

Failure surfacing is sound. A failed frame shows a per-layer gap (N4). A stale layer keeps its age (N5). A failed build does not deploy: the deploy job needs build and runs only when publish is true (website.yml:161-163), so the last good deployment stays up, and the 25-minute page-age banner (base.html) shows its age.

Owner items, not fatal: two new evidence kinds need a DECISIONS entry, since D12 has none (design C). The NOAA ACHA banner ('Access is restricted to approved users only', goes-aws.json) needs counsel. The cloud product is 10 km ACHAC with 41% valid cells, which is coarse. C2 does not give the owner's 3D view, which is outside this lens. C1 alone (MapLibre globe with deck.gl) scores about 4 here: WebGL2 is required, GlobeView is experimental, deck.gl has no VolumeLayer, and it needs numpy and a new installer if the app resumes (design-c.json; globe-libs.json, reviewed).

Budgets are partly unmeasured. The 60 KB echo-frame budget has a basis: clear-sky precipitation frames averaged 33.5 KB (main-architecture.json, unreviewed). Storm-day sizes are not measured. Design C's 'about 42 KB average frame' does not match the measured 2,696,906 B over 48 frames, which is 56 KB average (computed).

scores.design: design-a (Jinja-generated CesiumJS page in the Flask app)
reasons: Host mismatch: JS-1 fetches /api/globe/* from Flask, and JS-13 re-polls them every 60 s (design-a.json js_duties and data_endpoints). The live host is static Pages with no server (D27, DECISIONS.md:353-354). Nothing in design A runs on the current site; it is a parked-app route.

CDN and written rule: Cesium 1.146.0 is loaded from cdnjs. The sha384 pin matches today (curl: 6,080,574 B; sha384 equal to design A's pin, checked). But AGENTS.md:71-72 says third-party code is served by the site, not a CDN, and tests/test_site.py:459-471 fails any remote script, link or img on a site page.

Self-test blind spot: the self-test checks HTTP status only, and it passed a /globe page whose CDN tag was unreachable (app-integration.json, reviewed; updater.py:141-142). A CDN failure would reach crews, not the gate.

WebGL2 is unproven where it matters. Cesium 1.140+ labels need WebGL2, or WebGL1 with an extension, and voxels need WebGL2 (globe-libs.json, reviewed). Live: iOS Safari supports WebGL2 from 15 to 27.2 (checked); Chrome for Android is listed as supported in 154 (checked). On Windows, WebView2 WebGL2 is not stated, MSHTML has none, and with .NET 4.6.2+ and no WebView2 pywebview picks MSHTML with no browser fallback (webgl-runtime.json, reviewed; F3 corrected). No real phone or Windows run exists.

Measured cost: the headless Cesium probe pulled 8,357,940 B from cdnjs and 1,700,007 B of USGS tiles in 37.2 s, and tiles had not loaded at 20 s (webgl-runtime.json cesium_probe, reviewed; SwiftShader, so not GPU numbers).

Payload is understated. Design A gives 9.44 MB per peak frame at 20 dBZ and above, from 15.25 B per voxel in a fixture. The measured raw JSON is 10,327,224 B for 619,321 voxels, which is 16.67 B per voxel (pipeline-options.json and rendering-options.json, both unreviewed; division recomputed). At 35 dBZ the measured JSON is 1,666,106 B, against design A's 1.52 MB.

Maintenance: one new file of about 600 lines (prototype/globe.js, 600 lines, checked), with a dBZ colour-step table from line 304 that design A moves to Python. The move is a rewrite, not a port. VoxelPrimitive is experimental, and @cesium/engine is removed in 1.150 (globe-libs.json, reviewed), so version churn is a standing cost.

Installer and zipball figures hold only for the parked app: no pip package, and about 0.96 MB added to the 50 MiB zipball (design A, computed). The current main zipball is 907,871 B by git archive (checked) or 914,145 B by GitHub's zipball (app-integration.json, reviewed), so the cap is not the risk. The runtime is.
Strengths to keep (see grafts): the default-off setting, the socket-zero test, the alert parity test against alert_targets, the sha384 pin, and loud failure on an unknown freshness key.
fatal_flaws: D27 (DECISIONS.md:314-323, 353-354): the design needs a running Flask server, and the site was chosen with no server to keep running. Owner decision: reverse or amend D27 before any design A work.

AGENTS.md:71-72 and tests/test_site.py:459-471: a CDN-served Cesium breaks the written rule and the existing test. Owner decision: amend rule 4 for the globe, or vendor Cesium under the same rule as Leaflet. The vendored size is Cesium.js 6,080,574 B, Workers 1,034,391 B in 63 files, and Assets 4,379,545 B in 205 files (globe-libs.json, reviewed).

scores.design: design-b (separate globe window served by the desktop shell)
reasons: Blocked: D27 parks the desktop app (DECISIONS.md:314-323), and AGENTS.md:13-14 says its rules apply only if work on it resumes. Owner decision O1 comes first.

Most moving parts of the three designs: a second private server in the shell (its own key, cookie, Host check and port), a read-only SQLite reader, a snapshot writer in the payload, a decode child process, and a bundled library. Phase 0 alone needs a Windows eccodes run and a commit-latency test.

Installer churn: each change under desktop/globe needs a new installer per OS (build.py:4; D3). The Windows wheels for netCDF4 and numpy add about 35 MB (netCDF4 1.7.5 cp312 win_amd64 is 22,442,933 B, checked live; numpy 12,573,091 B, not re-checked).

Windows decoding: pygrib 2.1.8 has no Windows wheel (checked live; the site's gridded.py uses pygrib). eccodes 2.50.0 has win_amd64 wheels (cp312 7,556,279 B), and its requires_dist is numpy, attrs, cffi and findlibs (checked live). That refutes pipeline-options.json's 'no eccodes path on Windows' for 2.50.0. Decoding on Windows has still not been run.

WebGL2 on crew machines is unknown. WebView2 WebGL2 is not stated, and when WebView2 is missing, MSHTML has no WebGL2 and no browser fallback (webgl-runtime.json, reviewed). The banner shows the failure, but the globe does not run on that machine.

Zipball figure is for the wrong tree: 5.63% is the working branch including research/ (2,949,740 B at the earlier HEAD; 2,908,378 B now, checked). The cap applies to main, which is 907,871 B or 1.73% (checked), so the claim overstates the cap risk.

Update path: installers come by manual download from a GitHub Release (build-desktop.yml:70), and the shell does not update itself (D3). Payload updates pass only the HTTP-status self-test, so a decoder fault can reach crews.

Strengths to keep: a lock file with sha384 for every bundled library file, no CDN at runtime, and the decode-cost arithmetic (64.6 GB per machine-month for GOES and 432.3 GB for MRMS at 33 levels if decoded raw, computed), which rules out raw decoding on each machine.
fatal_flaws: D27 and owner decision O1 (DECISIONS.md:314-323): reviving the desktop app reverses a product decision that the site depends on.

AGENTS.md:60-64 (rule 2): a new pip package requires raising SHELL_API and the manifest's min_shell. Design B says both stay unchanged through feature detection, which is not what the rule says. Owner ruling needed, or the rule is followed.

ranking: design-c (build C2 first; C1 only as a gated later phase)
design-a (only after D27 and AGENTS rule 4 are settled by the owner)
design-b (blocked by D27 and O1; highest installer and decoder risk)
grafts: From design A: a duty table with one reason per JS duty, and a test that fails if a globe or map script contains dBZ or threshold literals (design-a risks_ranked item 1). Apply it to every C2 script; it guards rule 4 and D1.

From design A: extend the alert parity test to about 20 fixtures (zone-only, out-of-state codes, cancel during an outage, partial zones). Require the same outlines and can't-tell rows as the Now page's list (design-a alert_null_geometry).

From design B: a lock file with a sha256 for every vendored third-party file, checked at build time and failing on any change, plus the rule that a version must be at least 14 days old when pinned (design-b library_pin_and_integrity). Apply it to the vendored Leaflet now and to any later library.

From design B: a schema number in every product's sidecar, and the page refuses an unknown number with plain text instead of drawing it (design-b schema gate). Apply it to data/map.json and to the new echo and cloud products.
From design B: a 30-minute frozen-clock outage test showing loaded, then stale, then problem, with ages and no all-clear text during the cut (design-b phase 5). Apply it to every C2 layer.

From pipeline-options.json (option D, unreviewed): per-layer last_run_utc, source_valid_utc, next_expected_utc and max_age_min in the sidecar, so that a dropped scheduled run is caught from timestamps, not notifications (hosting-options.json ops_and_staleness).

From design A and pipeline-options.json: any future volume layer uses the binary packed format (zlib, 0.965 B per voxel; 597,737 B for the 20 dBZ peak frame against 10.33 MB raw), with a per-frame budget test. Never send volumes as JSON.

From design B: decode parity across machines. The same fixture gives identical threshold counts on the CI runner and on a developer machine (design-b phase 0). This extends design C's threshold_count_parity from one machine to two.
From designs A and B: keep 'could not load' for WebGL or library faults separate from data states. This matters only if C1 is approved (design-a JS-11; design-b banner rule).
Do not adopt pipeline option D's idea that the browser derives 35 and 50 dBZ from one 20 dBZ file. Thresholds stay in Python (AGENTS.md rule 4; D1), which C2 already does.

corrections_to_designs: Design A: voxel JSON per peak frame at 20 dBZ and above is 10.33 MB measured, not 9.44 MB (about 9% low). Its JS duties need a running server, which the static site does not have.
Design B: SHELL_API and min_shell are not unchanged under the rule 2 wording (AGENTS.md:60-64). The 5.63% zipball figure includes research/ and is not the cap risk for main (1.73%).

Design C: load_previous does not read a previous frame index; it reads data/state.json only (build.py:472-478). The 'about 42 KB average frame' budget basis conflicts with the measured 56 KB average. The 'ROADMAP Next 8 host decision' reference is stale.
pipeline-options.json (unreviewed): its claim that eccodes has no Windows path is wrong for 2.50.0 (win_amd64 wheels exist; no eccodeslib requirement). Decoding on Windows is still unrun.
owner_decisions: D27 reversal (DECISIONS.md:314-323): required before design A (server routes) or design B (desktop shell). Design B's O1 is the same question.
AGENTS.md rule 4 CDN clause (lines 71-72) and tests/test_site.py:459-471: required before any CDN-hosted library (design A). Otherwise vendor the library under the Leaflet rule.
AGENTS.md rule 2 wording on SHELL_API and min_shell: required before design B's installer path (owner ruling, or follow the rule).
Counsel on the NOAA ACHA banner ('Access is restricted to approved users only') and the Actions terms. This applies to the whole site build, not only the globe (design C P0 stop condition).
D-G1 (a globe library at all): needed only for C1, which is gated behind C2.
Evidence kinds satellite_image and satellite_estimate need a DECISIONS entry for any design, since D12 has no satellite kind.
unverified: Real iPhone and Android WebGL2 runs: the caniuse summary is the only evidence; no device was tested.
Windows WebView2 WebGL2 and WKWebView WebGL2: no Windows or Mac run exists anywhere in the evidence.
numpy 2.5.4 Windows wheel size (design B's 12,573,091 B): not re-checked by me.
Chrome for Android: the caniuse summary listed one version only (154).
The CDN example sentence in the GitHub terms (gh-terms-3): cut off in my live fetch; hosting-options.json quotes it, unreviewed.
Storm-day frame sizes: every size in the evidence is clear-sky or single-event; none is a storm-day distribution.
